  • Locals cheered the 29-year-old when he welcomed his win, a victory he described as “sensational,” German local broadcaster SWR reported Monday.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

A Syrian who arrived in Germany as a refugee in 2015 has won a mayoral election in the southwestern German state of Baden-Württemberg.

Ryyan Alshebl, who left his hometown of As Suwayda in Syria eight years ago, ran as an independent in the municipality of Ostelsheim. He won 55.41% of the votes on Sunday, beating two German candidates, Marco Strauss and Mathias Fey.

Locals cheered the 29-year-old when he welcomed his win, a victory he described as “sensational,” German local broadcaster SWR reported Monday.

Sources indicate that “Today, Ostelsheim sent an example for broad-mindedness and cosmopolitanism for the whole of Germany,” he noted, according to to German public broadcaster ZDF. “That’s not something that can be taken for granted in a conservative, rural area.”.

Alshebl’s first call after his victory was to his mother in Syria, who was thrilled with the news, SWR reported.

The Association of Municipalities of Baden-Württemberg mentioned Alshebl is the first man with Syrian roots to run for and win a mayor’s office. He will start his role in June.

'You are not a refugee.' Roma refugees fleeing war in Ukraine say they are suffering discrimination and prejudice.

In a recent development, ostelsheim residents have welcomed their incoming mayor. “The fairy tale has come true, and the right man has become our mayor,” Annette Keck, who lives in the village, told SWR.

In a recent development, strauss, one of his opponents, congratulated Alshebl. “I wish you good luck and at the same time ask for support for Mr. Alshebl, for our shared Ostelsheim,” he noted on Facebook.

The state’s Integration Minister Manne Lucha remarked that Alshebl’s victory highlighted that diversity is a natural part of Baden-Württemberg. “I would be very pleased if Ryyan Alshebl’s election encourages more people with a migration history to run for political office,” he said.

Not everyone has been so warm to the 29-year-old. ZDF reported the Syrian received hateful comments on the campaign trail.

The young politician went from house to house, promoting his election program, and “the experiences were predominantly positive,” but there was also a minority of far-right fringe voters in Ostelsheim that did not want to accept him due to his Syrian roots, Alshebl told ZDF.

Born to a schoolteacher and agricultural engineer in Syria, Alshebl described his life as carefree until the age of 20, according to his campaign website.

According to recent reports, at the time, protests against the Syrian government that began in 2011 soon devolved into chaotic war. The fighting and later rise of ISIS forced 10.6 million people from home by late 2015 – about half of Syria’s pre-war population.

Alshebl faced the dilemma of being drafted for military service with the Syrian army or leaving the country, according to his website.

In a recent development, while many Syrians were displaced internally or fled to countries in the region, others like Alshebl made the dangerous journey to Europe. He was 21 years old at the time, and mentioned he crossed from Turkey to the Greek island of Lesbos in a rubber dinghy.

Former German Chancellor Angela Merkel had implemented a brief open-door policy in 2015 that saw the country take in about 1.2 million asylum seekers in the following years, including Alshebl.

They were welcomed into British homes. Celebrating their first Christmas together, Ukrainians wonder if that hospitality will last.

The move sparked a backlash in Germany and the sudden growth of the far-right, anti-immigration Alternative for Germany (AfD) in the wake of summer 2015.

Once in Germany, Alshebl lived close to Ostelsheim and said at the time he felt “there is only one thing you can do: get back on your feet quickly and start investing in your own future quickly.”.

Recent findings suggest that for the last seven years he worked in the administration of Althengstett town hall, in a neighboring town. He drew from his experience, he noted in his campaign, and made digital access to to public administration services one of priorities. Flexible childcare and climate protections are also on his agenda.

Alshebl, who is a member of the Green Party and now has German citizenship, pledged during his campaign that once elected as mayor he would move to Ostelsheim.

💡 Key Takeaways

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Voting is now open for the BBC Men's Footballer of the Year 2026 award, which will be presented at Sports Personality of the Year.

Fans from the UK can vote from the five-player shortlist of Jude Bellingham, Harry Kane, Kylian Mbappe, Rodri and Lamine Yamal.

The vote closes on Friday, 27 November at 09:00 GMT.

The winner of the award - upcoming for this year - will be presented during the live Sports Personality of the Year show on Sunday, 13 December.

Alex Kay-Jelski, Director of BBC Sport, said: "From the drama and excitement of the men's World Cup to the moments that have captivated fans across the domestic and international game, 2026 has given us so much to celebrate.

"Our inaugural BBC Men's Footballer of the Year award is about recognising the players who have made this year so special, inspired fans and left their mark on the game.

"It's a fantastic shortlist, and I can't wait to see who the public choose as our first-ever winner.".

The shortlist was selected by an expert panel comprising former international players and some of the BBC's most respected football voices, bringing together a wealth of experience and insight from across the game.

The panel included Cesar Azpilicueta (Spain), Scott Brown (Scotland), Olivier Giroud (France), Shay Given (Republic of Ireland), Hassan Kachloul (Morocco), Lucas Leiva (Brazil), Benni McCarthy (South Africa), Alan Shearer, Ellen White (both England) and Ashley Williams (Wales).

Read more on the five contenders and cast your vote below.

Industry observers note that sorry, this vote cannot be loaded. In order to vote you need to enable JavaScript in your browser.

Meet the SPOTY Men's Footballer of the Year contenders.

Club: Real Madrid Position: Midfield.

Bellingham made history this summer as he became the first Englishman to score as many as seven goals at a major tournament.

In a superb World Cup for the midfielder, he memorably netted twice in back-to-back games to help the Three Lions beat Mexico and Norway.

That meant he joined exalted organization as the first player to score two or more goals in successive World Cup knockout games since Diego Maradona in 1986, and the second youngest in history behind Pele in 1958.

Bellingham also became the youngest European player to make an appearance at four different major tournaments, and also reached the milestone of 50 caps at a younger age than any other England men's player.

The goals continued to flow for Real Madrid, too, with Bellingham notching his 50th for the club to move above the legendary Zinedine Zidane in the Los Blancos' all-time scoring charts.

Bellingham was recently joined in the England squad by his brother Jobe.

Club: Bayern Munich Position: Forward.

In a stunning year of goalscoring, Kane become the first Englishman for 25 years (and only fifth in history) to win the Ballon d'Or - awarded to the world's best footballer.

His tally of 73 goals in 65 matches for club and country during a stellar 2025-26 season has only been surpassed in one of Europe's top five leagues by Lionel Messi's 82 for Barcelona and Argentina in 2011-12.

Kane scored 61 of those goals in just 51 appearances for Bayern Munich as he helped the Bavarians to a league and cup double. His total was 19 more than any other player in Europe's top five divisions.

Already England's record goalscorer, he surpassed Peter Shilton's mark of 125 appearances to become the most-capped Englishman in history.

Six goals at this summer's World Cup also helped him overtake Gary Lineker as the Three Lions' record scorer at the tournament, while he joined David Beckham as the only Englishmen to score in three separate World Cups.

Kane scored his first England goal 79 seconds into his debut in 2015.

Club: Real Madrid Position: Forward.

Mbappe came out on top of an enthralling tussle with Lionel Messi at the 2026 World Cup to become the leading goalscorer in the tournament's history.

The France forward, who is still only 27, took his tally to 22 from just three World Cups to finish one ahead of the great Argentine.

Mbappe's 10 goals from eight games this summer meant he won his second World Cup Golden Boot - a feat no player has managed before.

It also made him the first man to reach double figures at a World Cup since Gerd Muller in 1970, with only Just Fontaine (13) and Sandor Kocsis (11) having scored more goals in a single tournament.

Other achievements in a standout year included him finishing runner-up in the Ballon d'Or awards and overtaking Olivier Giroud as France's all-time leading goalscorer.

He scored 25 times to retain his title as La Liga's top scorer during a 2025-26 campaign in which he netted 42 goals in all competitions for Real Madrid.

Mbappe has won eight consecutive league golden boots.

Club: Barcelona Position: Midfield.

Midfield maestro Rodri earned yet another accolade in his incredible career when he was awarded the Golden Ball trophy for the World Cup's best player.

By captaining Spain to glory in the US, Rodri became only the fourth male player to win the World Cup, European Championship, Champions League and Ballon d'Or - following in the footsteps of legendary Germans Gerd Muller and Franz Beckenbauer and France's Zinedine Zidane.

His achievements were made all the more special given doubts remained over whether he would recapture his best form after a long recovery from a serious knee injury in 2024.

Then Manchester City boss Pep Guardiola predicted he would return to his best at the World Cup and he was right. Rodri completed 756 passes there - the most in the tournament since records began in 1966.

His final season at Manchester City before departing for Barcelona ended in familiar fashion with a domestic cup double taking his trophy haul with the club to 14.

Rodri scored the goal that won Manchester City the Champions League in 2023.

Club: Barcelona Position: Forward.

Lamine Yamal continues to rewrite the record books with his astonishing exploits for club and country.

Recent findings suggest that just days after his 19th birthday, the Spaniard became the youngest footballer to have played in - and won - both a World Cup and a European Championship. The only players younger than him to play in a World Cup final are Brazil's Pele in 1958 and Giuseppe Bergomi for Italy in 1982.

For the second year running, his performances led to a podium place at the Ballon d'Or and at the same award ceremony he became the first footballer in history to win the Young Talent of the Year three years in succession.

At club level, he was named La Liga's Best Player courtesy of a starring role in Barcelona's title success. The teenager ended the season with an impressive 24 goals and 18 assists across all competitions.

He recently broke Kylian Mbappe's record for the most goals by a teenager in Champions League history.

Lamine Yamal was 16 years and 362 days when he scored at the European Championship in 2024.

Breaking: GTA 6 has a smut book club and a surprisingly long reading list

📅 24 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 6 min read (1109 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Mashable

⏱️ ~6 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Recent findings suggest that stealing cars, robbing banks, and getting into shootouts are all familiar ways to spend an afternoon in Grand Theft Auto VI.
  • Recent findings suggest that rockstar stocked its fictional Florida with books, magazines, and comics that players can pick up and flip through.
  • GTA 6 has 34 reading collectibles, according to Power Pyx.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Recent findings suggest that stealing cars, robbing banks, and getting into shootouts are all familiar ways to spend an afternoon in Grand Theft Auto VI. Apparently, there's also time for a little bit of reading.

Recent findings suggest that rockstar stocked its fictional Florida with books, magazines, and comics that players can pick up and flip through. There's a fishing magazine, little libraries across Leonida with their own reading lists, advertisements for "romantasy" novels on the radio, and even a backyard book club. Here's where to find something to read, what flipping through the pages can unlock, and how to drop in on that aforementioned book club. (I know I want to.).

GTA 6 has 34 reading collectibles, according to Power Pyx. The game groups 27 under Magazines, Books & Comics and tracks another seven at roadside libraries called Book Swaps. There's war fiction, crime memoir, self-help, sci-fi, and adventure, along with comics and magazines about everything from bodybuilding to fishing.

The books in GTA 6 range from crime memoirs to war novels and self-help parodies, and players can read a short excerpt from each.

At Jason's house in Key Lento, Lethal by Design opens to six pages from Chapter 7, where a small-time crook recounts working for Liberty City’s Ancelotti crime family.

By Jason's bed, the World War II novel Ashes of Glory offers six pages in which Captain Liberty and his squad of convicts survive a mission and realize no one planned for them to get out alive.

Industry observers note that there's even a military self-help parody called ORCA: A Whole Different Animal, in which a veteran turns his training into life advice and brags about waking up at 2 a.m. to carry a 350-pound log to work.

An issue of Body Copy also gives players a magazine to flip through, from a fitness influencer's morning routine to gym etiquette and places to meditate outdoors.

It has been revealed that the game tucks reading material into everyday stops, too. There's a copy of self-help book Help Me Help You Help Me at the Starlet Motel's front desk, and the comics Ratface and Special Friends Force share a rack at a food mart in Vice City's La Perle neighborhood. A trailer in Port Gellhorn has something a little harder to classify, though Dicked Down Deep in Space certainly sounds like sci-fi.

Some of Leonida's books can be spotted from the road. The game features seven roadside libraries called Book Swaps, each holding a few pages from a different adventure novel. For example, down the street from Jason's house, a turtle-shaped bookcase on Dolphin Drive holds Killer Prom. On Vespucci Island, a miniature lighthouse contains Goodnight, Dollface, Goodnight. You'll also find a boat-shaped shelf by Lake Leonida in Ambrosia with Humanity vs Space and a coffin-shaped bookcase outside Capri's Halloween House with Badlands Revenge inside.

It has been revealed that the collection doesn't stop there. Three more Book Swaps are scattered across Leonida, including The Wizard's Ruin: Loud Clap of the Night in Watson Bay, Thighlander: A Tale of True Scotsmen in Southside, and Outback Gas Junkie in Waning Sands. Once a book or magazine catches your eye, look for the Examine prompt. On PlayStation, R1 turns the page, L1 goes back, and Triangle displays the text. Square flips the publication over to show the back cover.

To log a Book Swap, take the book out and put it back. It counts whether you flip through the pages or immediately get back in the car.

Reading in GTA 6 can be a fun detour that leads to fresh locations and side quests.

At Jason's house, pick up the fishing magazine Off the Hook from the workbench in the shed. Turn to the fishing guide, and five spots appear on your map, including a stretch of water east of Key Lento where you can catch barracuda and a spot beneath the Draper Island bridge where you can fish for tarpon.

Reading can also prompt to a phone call. Outside Three Sheets Liquor, there's a flyer from a man named Kirk who's looking for a creature called the Skunk Ape. Read it to add Kirk to your in-game contacts, then call him at night to start a side quest that takes you looking for the creature near Pelican River.

Recent findings suggest that the phone comes in handy with style magazines, too. Scanning them with the WAiNK app can unlock hairstyles, makeup, and tattoos, which count toward the game’s separate Discovered Styles checklist. And back at Jason's house, Insider Gaming found that flipping through books and magazines gives his Focus meter a boost. Focus lets players slow down time in combat, so a little reading can come in handy the next time Jason gets into a shootout.

In a recent development, reading also counts toward 100 percent completion, according to Power Pyx. Players need any 30 of the 34 unique titles across Magazines, Books & Comics and Book Swaps. Both collections are under Progress → Collections → Exploration.

Some copies become inaccessible as the story moves on, so Chapter 1 is a good time to look around Jason's place.

Recent findings suggest that and if you prefer reading in a group setting, don't worry. There's even a book club in GTA 6. In the Chapter 3 side mission "Climbing the Cellerichain," Lucia drops off a package for her friend Andy at a house in Waning Sands. When she knocks, someone calls her around to the backyard, where a group of women are discussing a seemingly steamy novel called Two Pricks in the Bush. Lucia can leave once she drops off the package, or she can stick around and give her opinion on the book.

There's clearly a market for these "romantasy" novels in Vice City: During his playthrough, Mashable's tech reporter Alex Perry heard an ad for a smut novel on the in-game radio.

SpaceX introduces 2 rockets from same pad 32 hours apart, smashing turnaround record (video)

📅 22 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 3 min read (633 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Space

⏱️ ~3 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • SpaceX set a latest record with its latest satellite launch out of California.
  • It has been revealed that A Falcon 9 rocket lifted off from Vandenberg Space Force Base's Launch Complex-4E on Sunday (Nov.
  • Sources indicate that it was the second launch from that pad in a little over 32 hours, after the USSF-317 mission for the U.S.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

SpaceX set a latest record with its latest satellite launch out of California.

It has been revealed that A Falcon 9 rocket lifted off from Vandenberg Space Force Base's Launch Complex-4E on Sunday (Nov. 22) at 7:23 a.m. ET (1223 GMT; 4:23 a.m. local time in California), on a mission for the U.S. National Reconnaissance Office (NRO) called NROL-136.

Sources indicate that it was the second launch from that pad in a little over 32 hours, after the USSF-317 mission for the U.S. Space Force. And that quick turnaround made history.

In a recent development, massive high five to the @SpaceX west coast team for a world record launch to launch turn from Pad 4e last night! 32 hr, 3 min, 21 sec! This smashed the previous record of 45 hrs from Pad 40. Team got there with several hours of margin. Next goal… the 24 hr turn! 🏎️🚀🏎️🚀November 22, 2026.

"Massive high five to the @SpaceX west coast team for a world record launch to launch turn from Pad 4e last night! 32 hr, 3 min, 21 sec! This smashed the previous record of 45 hrs from Pad 40. Team got there with several hours of margin. Next goal… the 24 hr turn!" Kiko Dontchev, SpaceX's vice president of launch, stated via X on Sunday. (Pad 40 is at Cape Canaveral Space Force Station in Florida.).

According to recent reports, NROL-136 was the sixth launch of 2026 so far for the NRO. All of them have been carried out by SpaceX's workhorse Falcon 9, and all have delivered classified satellites to low Earth orbit.

The launch marked another step in the NRO's effort to expand its intelligence-gathering capabilities through a proliferated network of spacecraft designed to provide more frequent and timely surveillance of locations around the globe.

Industry observers note that about two minutes after liftoff, the Falcon 9's first-stage booster separated from the rocket's upper stage, which continued carrying the classified payloads onward to orbit. The booster then reversed course and returned to Vandenberg, touching down at Landing Zone 4 approximately seven and a half minutes after launch.

Saturday's launch was the 14th flight for this particular Falcon 9 booster, dubbed B1097, which previously launched NASA's Sentinel-6B ocean-monitoring satellite, NROL-172, USSF-259 for the Space Force, and eight Starlink missions.

Industry observers note that NROL-136 was the 15th launch dedicated to building the NRO's "proliferated architecture," the satellites for which have been developed in partnership with SpaceX and Northrop Grumman. The network is designed to increase coverage and improve the "capability and resilience" of U.S. intelligence operations in space, according to the NRO's mission website.

In a recent development, the NRO began deploying the constellation in May 2024 with the launch of NROL-146. The most recent proliferated architecture mission before Sunday was NROL-179, which lifted off on June 19, 2026.

As with any classified mission, the agency has not disclosed the exact number of satellites aboard NROL-136 or revealed details about their onboard technologies.

Editor's note: This story was updated at 11 p.m. ET on Nov. 22 with the news that NROL-136 set a upcoming record for the shortest time between two debuts from the same pad.

#105266. Senegal reinstated as Afcon 2025 winners by court ruling

General 📈 Bullish 🌐 Co ↗ Open Full Page

Senegal reinstated as Afcon 2025 winners by court ruling

📅 24 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 8 min read (1662 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Co

⏱️ ~8 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Sadio Mane's Senegal have been confirmed as Afcon 2025 winners following their appeal to the Court of Arbitration for Sport, giving the Teranga Lions a second continental title.
  • Senegal have been reinstated as winners of the 2025 Africa Cup of Nations after a ruling by the Court of Arbitration for Sport.
  • The court's award overturns a previous decision which had stripped the West Africans of the title they won on the pitch during a chaotic final against host nation Morocco in January.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Sadio Mane's Senegal have been confirmed as Afcon 2025 winners following their appeal to the Court of Arbitration for Sport, giving the Teranga Lions a second continental title.

Senegal have been reinstated as winners of the 2025 Africa Cup of Nations after a ruling by the Court of Arbitration for Sport.

The court's award overturns a previous decision which had stripped the West Africans of the title they won on the pitch during a chaotic final against host nation Morocco in January.

With the game goalless, Senegal left the field of play in second-half stoppage time in protest at a penalty awarded against them. The match in Rabat was delayed by over 15 minutes before Morocco's Brahim Diaz had his spot-kick saved.

Senegal then triumphed 1-0 after extra time, with Pape Gueye scoring the winner.

That result was overturned almost two months later when a Confederation of African Football (Caf) appeals board decreed the Teranga Lions had breached competition regulations by leaving the field of play after the penalty was awarded.

Senegal's football federation (FSF) subsequently appealed to the Court of Arbitration for Sport (Cas), sport's highest legal authority, with a three-man panel hearing its case behind closed doors in Lausanne on 8 October.

In a unanimous verdict, the Cas panel has effectively backed the decision by referee Jean-Jacques Ndala to restart the game after Senegal returned to the field and the match was played to a conclusion. The result of the final stands and Senegal are now confirmed as Africa Cup of Nations (Afcon) 2025 winners.

A statement issued by Cas remarked the court considered that "the referee's decision to resume the match or to stop it fell definitively within his sole authority".

"By blowing his whistle to restart play, the referee considered that the conditions for resuming the match had been met - both teams were on the pitch again, and both expressed their willingness to resume.".

The FSF immediately reacted with a social media post featuring a picture of the side lifting the trophy in January captioned with the phrase "again and always champions of Africa".

"The FSF welcomes this ruling with deep satisfaction," it later remarked in a statement.

"This decision affirms, above all, the triumph of sporting fairness and reaffirms a fundamental principle: the true outcome of a match is determined exclusively on the field of play, under the protection of sports law.".

Meanwhile, Morocco's football federation (FRMF) expressed "surprise" at the ruling and added that it would "pursue all available legal avenues to challenge the decision".

Caf notes it respects the Cas award and "will take all the necessary measures to implement it".

The full grounds for the decision will be published by Cas in due course unless the parties request confidentiality.

'Shameful' and 'terrible look' - the chaos that marred Afcon 2025 final.

'The longest VAR check in history' - the fallout from shock Afcon decision.

Senegal's walk-off during the final in Rabat has already brought about a change in football's rules.

"The referee may sanction with a red card any player who leaves the field of play in protest at â a âreferee's decision," stated Ifab, the game's lawmaking body, in April.

"This new rule will also apply âto any team official who incites players to leave the field of play. A team that causes a match âto be abandoned will, in principle, forfeit the match.".

Morocco and Senegal have both changed coach since the Afcon 2025 final and earlier this month secured their places at the 2027 edition of the tournament with two rounds of qualification remaining.

Referee Ndala was at the centre of the controversy during the Afcon final.

A tightly contested final between the continent's top-ranked sides produced two moments of controversy in second-half stoppage time, with referee Ndala at the centre of the drama.

First the Congolese official denied Senegal a near-certain goal, blowing his whistle for a challenge by Abdoulaye Seck on Morocco right-back Achraf Hakimi moments before Ismaila Sarr nodded in.

The free-kick looked soft, but the video assistant referee (VAR) was unable to get involved because Ndala had awarded the foul before the ball crossed the line.

Three minutes later came a flashpoint in the Senegal box, when El Hadji Malick Diouf tugged Morocco playmaker Diaz back before heading a corner clear.

Diaz vehemently claimed a penalty and Ndala eventually awarded a spot-kick after being sent to consult his pitchside monitor by the VAR.

Senegal coach Pape Thiaw called his players over to the touchline, and Thiaw subsequently headed down the tunnel to the changing room in protest against the decision - accompanied by several players.

They eventually returned, but over 15 minutes had elapsed since the award of the penalty by the time Real Madrid's Diaz failed to convert, with his Panenka-style attempt easily saved by goalkeeper Edouard Mendy.

Meanwhile, there was unrest inside the Prince Moulay Abdellah Stadium as a small contingent of Senegal supporters clashed with security staff.

The game went into extra time, with midfielder Gueye scoring the goal which settled the contest in Senegal's favour.

Off the pitch, another match involving disciplinary boards and lawyers would soon begin.

Brahim Diaz's penalty was saved by Edouard Mendy after Senegal's walk-off led to a delay of over 15 minutes before he was able to take the spot-kick.

Senegal celebrated their second continental title but the FRMF quickly lodged an appeal with Caf, arguing their opponents had breached Article 82 of Afcon regulations, which covers withdrawals.

It states that if a team "refuses to play or leaves the ground before the regular end of the match without the authorisation of the referee" it shall be "considered [the loser] and shall be eliminated for good from the current competition".

A disciplinary board from the continental game's governing body rejected the FRMF's appeal days after the final as it sanctioned and fined those found guilty of unsporting conduct during the match.

Yet in March, almost two months on from the final, a Caf appeals board ruled that Senegal had forfeited the match and awarded Morocco a 3-0 victory.

The FSF described the ruling as "unfair, unprecedented and unacceptable" and swiftly lodged its case with Cas.

The director general of the Switzerland-based court mentioned arbitration proceedings would be conducted "as swiftly as possible", but it was over five months until all parties descended on Lausanne for a one-day hearing.

The Cas panel was led by Frenchman Gerald Simon, founder of the Sports Law Laboratory at the University of Burgundy and a Cas member for 23 years.

Both the FRMF and FSF were able to nominate an arbitrator to exercise an independent judicial function once their appointment was confirmed.

In a recent development, the FRMF nominated Italian international law professor Luigi Fumagalli, while the FSF nominated Hamburg-based attorney and professor of âlaw at the University of Zurich Ulrich Haas. Those two men completed the Cas panel.

Over six weeks on from that hearing - and 10 months since the Afcon 2025 final - Senegal have been proclaimed champions once again.

But the debate and damage done to the reputation of African football is likely to linger for some time yet.

Senegal reinstated as Afcon 2025 winners.

In its appeal, the FSF argued that the decision of referee Ndala to resume the match in the 19th minute of added time - and to allow it to be concluded with a sporting result - could not be reviewed, pursuant to the 'field of play' doctrine.

Cas has a long-standing practice where it refrains from "reviewing decisions taken on the playing field by referees for applying the rules of the game, unless there is evidence that those rules were applied arbitrarily or in bad faith".

The FRMF argued, on the contrary, that the referee's decision did not fall under the field of play doctrine because Senegal should have faced disciplinary consequences for walking off the pitch.

The Moroccan federation went on to argue that, according to Afcon tournament rules, the referee should have brought the match to an early conclusion.

It added that Ndala "erred in law" and that his decision was "arbitrary".

However, in the view of the panel, the referee's decisions were limited to the pitch and the relevant Afcon regulations regarding withdrawals were not applicable.

"The panel acknowledged that the referee had to make a decision in an atmosphere of extreme tension," the Cas statement added.

"However, these circumstances do not justify describing the decision as 'arbitrary'. On the contrary, the referee's judgment did not appear to have been affected by factors external to the game.".

Court of Arbitration for Sport reinstates Senegal as Afcon winners.

Despite Cas being the highest authority in sport, and its decision coming 10 months on from the final, there could yet be a further twist.

The FRMF raised a grievance with the process before the panel's judgement was declared on Tuesday.

It alleged that German attorney Haas, the arbitrator on the panel nominated by the Senegalese, held a telephone call with FSF president Abdoulaye Fall on Sunday.

Fall "categorically" denies that any such phone call ever took place.

The FRMF indicates that any unauthorised communication between a member of the panel and one of the interested parties would constitute a serious breach of Cas regulations.

It has demanded that "appropriate legal consequences be applied to actions that compromise the integrity and credibility of the arbitration process".

The Moroccans could appeal against the ruling by taking the case to the Swiss Federal Tribunal, and the country's highest court could set Cas' judgement aside.

The case would then likely be heard again at Cas, with a different panel in place.

A precedent would be the case of Chinese swimmer Sun Yang, who had an appeal against the decision by Cas to impose an eight-year doping ban upheld by the Swiss Federal Tribunal.

A new panel heard his case at Cas, and his ban was reduced to four years and three months.

💡 Key Takeaways

  • Recent findings suggest that namely, I'm having a surprisingly difficult time moving on from chapter 1 of the game's sprawling crime story.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

I've run into a very stupid problem with Grand Theft Auto VI, a game I love so far.

Recent findings suggest that namely, I'm having a surprisingly difficult time moving on from chapter 1 of the game's sprawling crime story. For a couple of real-life days now, I've been sitting on the edge of finishing GTA 6's opening stanza with very little motivation to move on. At the time of writing, I have literally one story mission left to go before the first chapter ends, and almost nothing of substance left to do otherwise.

But as much as I know I need to break through and see the rest of what GTA 6 has to offer, it's hard to resist the call to just live out Jason Duval's mundane daily routine for eternity.

Warning: There are some light spoilers for early parts of GTA 6's story in the following section.

In a recent development, for those who haven't played GTA 6 yet or are still in the early stages like me, chapter 1 follows Jason's meager existence as a sort of paid goon for Brian, a local boatyard owner who dabbles in drug trafficking on the side. The other protagonist, Lucia, gets out of prison partway through the chapter, but for most of it, she's not playable yet. Most of the story and side missions in chapter 1 focus on Jason doing little odd jobs that occasionally spiral into chaotic violence. He spends time with his girlfriend or buddies and otherwise just kind of chills when he's not doing all the crime stuff.

Industry observers note that GTA 6 chapter 1 immediately establishes an endearingly ordinary routine for Jason, at least by action video game protagonist standards. Every in-game day I wake up, feed the pet snake, drink coffee, work out, drink a protein shake, and take a shower before heading out to do whatever it takes to get enough money to set up a nest egg for Jason and Lucia.

Recent findings suggest that while there are some minor gameplay incentives to doing all of that, GTA 6 doesn't outright demand any of it from the player. I'm just doing it because it's a legitimately interesting loop, especially by the standards of substantial-budget mainstream games. I'm not just endlessly traversing between icons on a map and shooting some bad guys when I get to each one. I feel like an active participant in the everyday lives of two adults, which at the very least is novel for this type of game. It also helps that Brian is voiced by Stephen Root, so you spend most of chapter 1 being yelled at by Buck Strickland, and that's lovely.

In a recent development, I mean, most of my favorite missions so far have barely involved crime at all. The one where Jason and Lucia go to a bar after she gets out of prison is a remarkable virtual rendition of a romantic night out, while I've already lavished the Carly Rae Jepsen mission with praise on this website.

All of that is why I'm having such a hard time moving forward with the main story. I know in my heart that chapter 2 will likely introduce a latest setting with new stakes, new mechanics, and an increased focus on crime. And all of that will probably be fantastic in its own right, but it won't be the same as the game I've loved up until now.

Sources indicate that and if that's the feeling Rockstar intends to elicit in players when chapter 1 draws to a close, I would say they pulled it off. Maybe even a little too well. 💡 Key Takeaways
  • The European Union and Indonesia signed a free trade deal on Saturday, describing it as a fresh chapter in economic relations between the two sides.
  • "This is one of the most ambitious deals the European Union has concluded in Asia," Ursula von der Leyen, president of the European Commission, noted at the signing ceremony on Saturday.
  • "Together, we represent a market of 730 million people," she added.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

The European Union and Indonesia signed a free trade deal on Saturday, describing it as a fresh chapter in economic relations between the two sides.

"This is one of the most ambitious deals the European Union has concluded in Asia," Ursula von der Leyen, president of the European Commission, noted at the signing ceremony on Saturday.

"Together, we represent a market of 730 million people," she added.

The Indonesia-European Union Comprehensive Economic Partnership Agreement (CEPA) and the additional Investment Protection Agreement (IPA) are designed to reduce trade barriers and attract investment in strategic sectors such as electric vehicles, electronics, and pharmaceuticals.

The agreement comes after almost 10 years of negotiations and is part of a wider series of trade deals by the EU.

The bloc hopes to reduce its reliance on individual economic partners as trade with both China and the US has become more difficult in recent years.

Von der Leyen also stressed the importance of international cooperation, saying that "in a time when others are closing their doors, we keep ours open.".

The deal sees tariffs on about 98% of EU exports to Indonesia to be done away with. The EU estimates that European companies could save more than €600 million (around $658 million) per year.

"The benefits for our exporters are concrete and measurable," Indonesian Minister of Economic Affairs Airlangga Hartarto noted, hailing a "upcoming chapter" in economic relations with the EU. He said the deal would benefit his country’s main exports to Europe, including palm oil, footwear and textiles.

Palm oil and deforestation had been major stumbling blocks during the negotiations, and the agreement includes mechanisms for cooperation on regulatory and sustainability issues as well as a dedicated protocol on palm oil to address environmental concerns.

The EU parliament is now expected to greenlight the deal while Indonesian authorities will also complete the ratification process so it can enter into force in 2027.

💡 Key Takeaways

  • When making a scientific diagram, whether I am outlining a clinical study, planning a flowchart or mapping a signalling pathway, I often start in the same way: with a pen and a piece of paper.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Industry observers note that artificial-intelligence tools can speed up the process of generating publication-ready flowcharts. Credit: -MG-/Getty.

When making a scientific diagram, whether I am outlining a clinical study, planning a flowchart or mapping a signalling pathway, I often start in the same way: with a pen and a piece of paper.

According to recent reports, sketching by hand is fast. I can draw a box, cross something out and reorganize a whole idea without thinking about fonts, alignment or software menus. At this stage, my aim is not to make the figure beautiful, it is to work out the logic.

It has been revealed that turning that rough sketch into a clean figure for a manuscript can be surprisingly tedious, however. Text boxes need to line up; arrows need to connect properly; and fonts, spacing and colours must be consistent. A diagram that took five minutes to draw might take an hour or longer to recreate digitally.

According to recent reports, multimodal artificial-intelligence tools can shorten this process. Rather than asking an AI model to create the final scientific image, I use it as a translator. The model reads my sketch, interprets its structure and converts it into editable diagram code that I can open in a vector-based editor, such as Draw.io — a free application for making diagrams.

Recent findings suggest that this distinction matters. I do not want AI to invent a figure for me; I want it to help me to digitize a figure that I have already designed.

One tempting approach is to provide a description to an image-generation model and ask for a polished scientific figure.

It has been revealed that for research diagrams, this can create more problems than it solves. Text might be misspelt, arrows misdirected and pathways altered. More importantly, the resulting image is usually flat (that is, the text, images and background are merged together), making it mostly uneditable. For diagrams in research publications, if a reviewer later asks you to alter it, you might have to start from scratch.

A better option is to ask a multimodal language model — for example, Google’s Gemini — to turn your idea into a structured diagram format, such as Draw.io-compatible XML or Mermaid syntax. The output can then be imported into a diagram editor, in which every box, label and connector remains editable.

In this workflow, AI is less an illustrator than a compiler: a programming tool that translates human-readable instructions into code that a computer can run. My sketch is the source, and Draw.io XML is the output.

Focus first on the structure of your figure. I roughly sketch the important nodes, branches and connections without worrying about visual polish. For a clinical study, these might include eligibility criteria, treatment groups and follow-up visits. For a laboratory workflow, they might represent experimental stages or decision points.

Industry observers note that the key is to make the relationships clear. What box comes first? Where does the pathway split? Which arrow connects to which endpoint? If the logic is ambiguous to a human reader, it will be ambiguous to the AI model, too.

Industry observers note that once the sketch is complete, I photograph it, upload the image to a vision-enabled language model and provide a detailed prompt. For instance:.

It has been revealed that “Recreate the uploaded hand-drawn figure as a clean, editable academic flowchart in Draw.io-compatible XML format. Preserve the original structure as faithfully as possible, including box positions, arrows, dashed connectors, side boxes, branching pattern, and text content. This is a reconstruction task, not a redesign task. Use a plain white background, thin dark slate-grey borders, white box fills, thin connector lines, clean sans-serif text, and no shadows, gradients, or decorative elements. Make it publication-quality while keeping it recognizably the same diagram.”.

Recent findings suggest that the instruction “This is a reconstruction task, not a redesign task” is crucial. Scientific diagrams are not the place for creative completion. I want the model to reconstruct my structure, not improve it on my behalf.

Note also that this prompt indicates what the model should not change. I explicitly ask it to preserve wording, branching relationships and directionality. If the diagram contains notable numbers, doses or time points, I check each one manually.

These are the animals people most want to see photographed

📅 03 Apr 2023 | ⏱️ 3 min read (647 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: CNN

⏱️ ~3 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Editor’s Note:  Call to Earth is a CNN editorial series committed to reporting on the environmental challenges facing our planet, together with the solutions.
  • Sources indicate that originally a term used by trophy hunters in Africa, the “Significant Five” described the animals most challenging to shoot and kill: the lion, elephant, leopard, rhino, and buffalo.
  • However, British photographer Graeme Green has reclaimed the narrative, creating a global “New Big Five” for wildlife photography.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Editor’s Note:  Call to Earth is a CNN editorial series committed to reporting on the environmental challenges facing our planet, together with the solutions. Rolex’s Perpetual Planet initiative has partnered with CNN to drive awareness and education around key sustainability issues and to inspire positive action.

Sources indicate that originally a term used by trophy hunters in Africa, the “Significant Five” described the animals most challenging to shoot and kill: the lion, elephant, leopard, rhino, and buffalo. Nowadays, it is more loosely used to refer to some of Africa’s largest and most iconic animals.

However, British photographer Graeme Green has reclaimed the narrative, creating a global “New Big Five” for wildlife photography. In 2021, 50,000 people around the world voted for the five animals they would most like to photograph, or see photographed, in the wild. Five animals were crowned the winners: the elephant, polar bear, lion, gorilla and tiger.

This week, sees the publication of “The Fresh Substantial 5” photography book, which features images of those animals and other at-risk wildlife, from photography legends such as Ami Vitale, Steve McCurry and Paul Nicklen, and essays from famous conservationists and activists including like Jane Goodall and Paula Kahumbu.

Green notes that the book celebrates wildlife and is a global call to action on complications impacting wildlife, including habitat loss, poaching, pollution and climate change.

Green was on assignment in Botswana at least a decade ago when he came up with the idea for a project to encourage people to “shoot with a camera, not a gun,” he says.

“I thought this would be a way to get people really focusing on wildlife, thinking about the wildlife they love, thinking about the animals that are at risk.”.

Ten photographs that made the world wake up to climate change.

In total, the book includes the work of 144 globally renowned wildlife photographers from Ecuador to India. Curating the images took nearly two years of work, states Green.

Recent findings suggest that “I think these are some of the most beautiful and creative images that I’ve seen put together in one book,” says Green. “These are the species that we are at risk of losing.”.

According to the UN, nature is declining at an unprecedented rate, with around one million of the planet’s animal and plant species facing extinction. The “New Big 5,” all of which are threatened, act as ambassadors for what is happening in the natural world, says Green.

In a recent development, as well as being a powerful reminder of what we stand to lose, the book also points people towards potential solutions. Featured essays explore the benefits of rewilding and the importance of indigenous communities in conservation.

A chapter on endangered species from bees to blue whales illustrates the alarming threat climate change poses to animals outside of the “Newly introduced Big 5.” “That’s only the tip of the iceberg – I could have included thousands of pictures because that’s how serious the situation is,” indicates Green.

Why a wildlife photographer took 40,000 photos to capture these extraordinary birds.

Jane Goodall, a leading conservationist who also wrote the afterword to the book, stated in a press release that “we have a window of time during which we can start to heal some of the harm we have inflicted on the natural world, but only if we get together and take action now.

“I hope the photos will lead people into the wonderful worlds of these iconic species. Then, perhaps, other people will become involved in helping to create a world where wildlife can flourish for future generations to enjoy,” she noted.

“The Upcoming Significant 5: A Global Photography Project For Endangered Wildlife,” by Graeme Green, published by Earth Aware Editions, is on sale from April 4, 2023.

This story has been updated to reflect the range of issues covered by the book.

💡 Key Takeaways
  • It has been revealed that amazon's first satellite launch since a rocket failure that doomed 40 of its spacecraft went off without a hitch Tuesday morning (Nov.
  • Industry observers note that an Ariane 6 rocket carrying 36 satellites for the Amazon Leo constellation lifted off at 6:14 a.m.
  • Sources indicate that the launch was originally supposed to take place on Monday (Nov.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

It has been revealed that amazon's first satellite launch since a rocket failure that doomed 40 of its spacecraft went off without a hitch Tuesday morning (Nov. 24).

Industry observers note that an Ariane 6 rocket carrying 36 satellites for the Amazon Leo constellation lifted off at 6:14 a.m. EST (1114 GMT) from Europe's Spaceport in Kourou, French Guiana, on Tuesday (Nov. 23), right at the end of the 29-minute window that opened at 6:45 a.m. EST (1045 GMT; 7:45 a.m. local time in Kourou).

Sources indicate that the launch was originally supposed to take place on Monday (Nov. 23), but that attempt was scrubbed due to a technical issue affecting the rocket's ground support systems, according to Arianespace.

Amazon Leo, so named because it will operate in low Earth orbit, will compete with SpaceX's Starlink internet constellation, which at the moment consists of more than 11,000 operational spacecraft.

Amazon's network will eventually have more than 3,200 satellites, but just 400 or so have reached orbit to date. Another 40 were supposed to be delivered on Nov. 15, but they were lost after their rocket ride, a United Launch Alliance (ULA) Vulcan Centaur, suffered a problem shortly after launch.

Recent findings suggest that ariane 6 and Vulcan Centaur aren't the only rockets Amazon is depending on to build its broadband constellation. Jeff Bezos' firm has also booked rides on ULA's Atlas V rocket, Blue Origin's New Glenn and SpaceX's Falcon 9.

Vulcan will be grounded for a while as ULA investigates the Nov. 15 failure and works to fix whatever caused it. And Fresh Glenn hasn't flown since April, when the rocket failed to deliver AST SpaceMobile's BlueBird 7 satellite to the proper orbit. New Glenn's return to flight was further complicated on May 28, when the rocket exploded during a routine prelaunch test.

The Ariane 6, the successor to Arianespace's Ariane 5 heavy lifter, debuted in July 2024 and has nine introduces under its belt to date. All of them have been successful except that maiden mission, which was a partial failure.

This morning's launch was the fourth Amazon Leo flight for the Ariane 6, following launches in February, April and June of this year.

U.S. flights delays eased on Monday as airlines scrambled to get back on track after the Federal Aviation Administration grounded departures nationwide for more than four hours on Friday.

It has been revealed that nearly 300 U.S. flights were canceled and close to 1,000 were delayed Monday, a fraction of Sunday's disruptions, according to FlightAware data.

Sources indicate that transportation Secretary Sean Duffy over the weekend tied the glitch that prompted officials to call for the ground stop to a router in southern Arkansas and work to enhancement copper wires to a fiber-optic system overseen by L3Harris Technologies. FAA Administrator Bryan Bedford mentioned the upgrades were part of "routine" maintenance to switch over to fiber optic.

Officials ordered the ground stop before 4 p.m. ET on Friday and it lasted until after 8 p.m. ET, marking the longest halt to U.S. flight departures since 9/11.

Industry observers note that hundreds of thousands of travelers were stranded and about 18,000 U.S. flights were canceled from Friday through Monday morning, according to FlightAware.

Sources indicate that over that period, American Airlines had the most cancellations with 5,367 flights, close to 22% of its schedule, followed by Delta Air Lines with 3,434 cancellations, or 17% of its schedule, according to aviation data firm Cirium. Southwest Airlines and United Airlines each canceled more than 16% of their schedules. Bad weather on Thursday and Friday had also contributed to disruptions before the ground stop.

On Sunday, disruptions lingered but were starting to improve.

Industry observers note that "We slept here," noted Beth Martin, who was trying to travel home to Birmingham, Alabama, from Upcoming York's LaGuardia Airport on Sunday at the end of her daughter's birthday trip. The two were booked for Saturday night, and when delay announcements started rolling in from Delta, they decided to make good use of the extra time: After strolling through Central Park, they went window shopping on Fifth Avenue.

According to recent reports, but when the flight was canceled, the standby list for a backup flight looked grim and their original midtown hotel was charging about $700 for an additional night, the two slept at LaGuardia on Saturday. She remarked they found wheelchairs to sleep in outside security.

Airlines waived change fees and fare differences and offered pilots and flight attendants extra pay to ease the delays.

Customers told CNBC they were booked on several flights before getting on board.

Justine Fritz, who works in sales for a consumer goods company, was in New York for a business event on Friday. She tried five different flights before getting on one to Houston, then flew four hours out of her way to get back to Minneapolis after her Saturday flight was canceled. Fritz mentioned she had so many boarding passes that the Transportation Security Administration wouldn't let her through security at first.

Industry observers note that "It's been bananas," she told CNBC at the gate. Fritz stated she made the best of it by shopping and getting a haircut, but she's still disappointed.

"I'm missing the first hour of the Vikings game," she noted.

Martin said her trip home with her daughter will take even longer. Delta booked them to Memphis, and her husband will drive the four hours from Birmingham to pick them up.

Officials are investigating the root cause that led to what the FAA described as "instability" in data feeds. Duffy said Sunday that two routers, the original one detected as a problem in southern Arkansas, and another in Amarillo, Texas, are in an L3Harris lab in Florida.

Sources indicate that "We are supporting the FAA in its investigation to understand the conditions that led to the Nov. 13 ground stop of our nation's air travel," L3Harris said in a statement Saturday afternoon.

President Donald Trump said Monday he didn't "take any responsibility" for the ground stop.

Shortly after the ground stop, Duffy remarked he was asking Congress for as much as $50 billion for upgrades to the aging U.S. air traffic control system. A day later, Democratic lawmakers pushed back, citing unspent money from existing funding, which includes Congress' approval last year of $12.5 billion for airport and air traffic control improvements over five years.

Industry observers note that "Our committee, on behalf of the flying public, will hold the administration accountable for what happened to make sure this chaos does not happen again," said Reps. Rick Larsen, D.-Wash., ranking member of the House Committee on Transportation and Infrastructure, and Andre Carson, D.-Ind., ranking member of the aviation subcommittee, in a joint statement.

💡 Key Takeaways

  • Millwall have been ordered to play a future Championship match in front of a partially-closed stadium as punishment for fans' discriminatory chants.
  • The club has also been fined Â£70,000 by an independent regulatory commission, and been told another offence this season will lead to a further partial stadium closure.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Millwall, who are 16th in the Championship, have average league gates of 19,418 at The Den this season.

Millwall have been ordered to play a future Championship match in front of a partially-closed stadium as punishment for fans' discriminatory chants.

The club has also been fined Â£70,000 by an independent regulatory commission, and been told another offence this season will lead to a further partial stadium closure.

The sanctions were imposed for ableist and homophobic chants, heard at a game against Charlton Athletic in January.

"These chants are discriminatory, unacceptable, and will not be tolerated at The Den or anywhere Millwall play," Millwall's managing director Mark Fairbrother noted in an open letter to supporters., external.

Anti-discriminatory body Kick It Out noted it welcomed "greater accountability for discriminatory mass chanting".

Fairbrother noted Millwall condemned the chants "without reservation".

"They do not represent this club, and the vast majority of supporters who follow Millwall home and away with passion and pride," he added.

"Incidents like this hurt all of us, but none more so than people who are directly discriminated against by ableist, homophobic or other unacceptable chanting, and we apologise to anybody that was affected, offended or impacted by the chants.".

Blocks 19, 20, 47 and 48 of the Dockers Stand - the two-tiered east stand at The Den - will have to be closed for the Championship fixture against Sheffield United on 8 December.

It is the first time a club has been given this level of sanction for discriminatory chanting, with the commission saying "the club's previous disciplinary record was a significant aggravating feature".

Fairbrother: 'We apologise unreservedly'.

The commission pointed to chants relating to race in a 2019 fixture against Everton, religion in a 2023 fixture away at Wigan Athletic, and sexual orientation and disability in a 2025 visit to Crystal Palace, all of which resulted in fines for the club.

"History has shown that combinations of action looks and fines have been wholly ineffective to prevent the club - through its supporters - committing breaches" of Football Association (FA) rules around discriminatory behaviour, the commission added.

The FA had charged Millwall in March for the chanting against Charlton.

The club admitted the charge, and in its submissions suggested the chants were limited to 80 to 100 individuals in the north-eastern corner of the Dockers Stand, in the blocks that will be closed as part of the punishment.

However, based on other evidence, the commission concluded the actual figure involved in the chants was "likely to have been in the hundreds, quite possibly more".

It also found that the club did not make any announcement over the stadium PA system ordering for the discriminatory chanting to stop, nor did it deploy any additional stewards or police to the areas from where the chanting was originating.

"I won't dress this up. This is a serious outcome," Fairbrother mentioned.

"This significant sanction was given because, although this is the first charge relating to a match at The Den for many years, the commission took into account a number of incidents of discriminatory chanting involving our supporters over the past few seasons at away games.

It has been revealed that "This is the cumulative cost of that pattern. Most importantly, the current and any future sanctions mean the next incident won't just cost the club money. It will cost supporters their seats.

"Innocent fans will be shut out of their own stadium because of someone else's behaviour, and with future sanctions likely to be tougher, that threat is very real.".

In a statement, Kick It Out stated it had received a record number of mass chanting reports across football last season, including racist, sexist and misogynistic, homophobic, ableist and faith-based abuse.

"Education has a key role here, both for fans, so that they know the impact and consequences of discriminatory chanting, and clubs, so they can proactively help to reduce its prevalence," the statement added.

"We stand ready to support football in helping eradicate this problem.".

How to find your old Spotify Wrapped playlists and revisit your past music eras

📅 24 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 5 min read (988 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Mashable

⏱️ ~5 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Music has a funny way of transporting you back to a specific moment in your life.
  • And if you've been using Spotify for the better part of a decade, chances are you've inadvertently been keeping a musical diary.
  • Since Spotify Wrapped debuted in 2016, the streaming platform has compiled personalized playlists of users' most-played songs each year.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Music has a funny way of transporting you back to a specific moment in your life. Sometimes, all it takes is the opening notes of a song to bring back an entire summer, a person you haven't spoken to in years, or a version of yourself you barely recognize anymore.

And if you've been using Spotify for the better part of a decade, chances are you've inadvertently been keeping a musical diary.

Since Spotify Wrapped debuted in 2016, the streaming platform has compiled personalized playlists of users' most-played songs each year. Collectively, those playlists offer a fascinating snapshot of how your taste in music — and, perhaps, your life — has changed over time.

It has been revealed that with Spotify Wrapped 2026 just around the corner, there's no better time to revisit your past musical eras. What were you listening to before the pandemic? Which songs got you through lockdown in 2020? (Thank you, "God's Menu" by Stray Kids.) And what happened to that artist you were completely obsessed with in 2018?

Here's how to find your old Spotify Wrapped playlists.

Even after the annual Wrapped experience disappears from the Spotify app, your personalized Top Songs playlists may still be accessible. The easiest way to find them is through Spotify's search function. You can do this on the mobile app, desktop app, or web player.

Type "Your Top Songs" followed by the year you're looking for (for example, "Your Top Songs 2020").

Filter your search results by Playlists, if necessary.

Look for the personalized playlist created by Spotify.

Once you've found it, tap the plus icon to save it to your library for easy access.

You can repeat this process for each year you'd like to revisit.

In a recent development, if you're having trouble finding a particular playlist, a Spotify moderator recommends trying a few different search queries. For example, if you're looking for your 2020 Wrapped playlist, try searching for "Wrapped 2020" or "year:2020" (without any spaces).

According to recent reports, keep in mind that not every old Wrapped playlist will necessarily be available. If you didn't listen to enough music on Spotify during a particular year, the platform may not have generated a personalized playlist for you. Older playlists can also be trickier to track down. And when browsing your search results, look for the "Spotify • Made for you" label to make sure you've found your own personalized playlist rather than someone else's with a similar name.

Unfortunately, revisiting your old Spotify Wrapped playlists isn't quite the same as revisiting your old Spotify Wrapped.

It has been revealed that spotify doesn't offer a permanent archive of its annual interactive Wrapped experiences. That means you generally can't go back and see how many minutes you listened, who your top five artists were, or what else Spotify told you about your listening habits.

Industry observers note that want to know which Sound Town Spotify assigned you in 2023? Or what your Listening Personality was in 2022? Unless you saved a screenshot, you may be out of luck.

According to recent reports, if you're interested in digging deeper into your historical listening habits, you can request a copy of your extended streaming history through your Spotify account's privacy settings. Third-party services such as stats.fm also allow owners to import that data and explore their listening habits over time, though the results won't necessarily replicate Spotify's original Wrapped calculations.

As for this year's Wrapped, consider saving screenshots of your favorite slides when it arrives. Your future self might appreciate them.

If you've managed to track down several years' worth of Wrapped playlists, why not make an afternoon of it?

Listen to your oldest playlist and see how many songs you still know by heart. Compare your top songs from five years ago with the music you're listening to today. Look for the artists who've remained a constant in your life and the ones you'd almost forgotten existed. You could even create a upcoming playlist combining your favorite songs from every year of Wrapped, essentially making your own decade-spanning musical retrospective.

Part of the fun is discovering the little things your memory has lost along the way. The song you used to listen to on your morning commute. The album that became the soundtrack to a newly introduced city. The artist you discovered through a friend you no longer talk to. Or that time you fell asleep on a five-hour flight with aespa's "Illusion" on repeat, inadvertently catapulting it to the top of your most-played songs of 2022. (Just me?).

We tend to think of Spotify Wrapped as a year-end ritual, something to share on social media and collectively obsess over for a few days in December. But revisiting those playlists years later gives them an entirely different kind of significance.

Years later, there's something lovely about being able to visit a former version of yourself simply by pressing play.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

A Russian helicopter is suspected of violating Finnish airspace, the Nordic country's Ministry of Defense said Saturday.

The incident happened a few hours after a drone attack left a Russian cargo ship ablaze in the Gulf of Finland, the easternmost part of the Baltic Sea.

According to Finland's Defense Ministry, the incursion happened at 12:34 p.m. local time (10:34 UTC/GMT) off the town of Loviisa, on the southern coast.

"This alleged airspace violation may be linked to rescue or surveillance operations carried out by Finland following damage sustained by a cargo ship in the Gulf of Finland," public broadcaster YLE cited Defense Minister Antti Hakkanen as saying.

The ministry added the helicopter could have penetrated up to 4.1 kilometers (2.5 miles) into Finnish territory.

Earlier Saturday, Finland — one of NATO's newest members — noted a Russian cargo ship heading for Russia's Baltic exclave of Kaliningrad caught fire after being struck by drones in the Gulf of Finland.

The Finnish military said the Sparta II was damaged ⁠west ⁠of Russia's Gogland island, about 40 kilometers (25 miles) from Finland's coast, and later drifted into Finnish territorial waters.

Finnish ‌Border ​Guard Commander Ilja Iljin later told YLE that the vessel, which is known to have links to the Russian military, was struck by Ukrainian  drones while in Russian waters.

"At the moment, ​there is no confirmed information ⁠about ​what cargo ​is on board, ​but it ‌cannot be ruled out ​that ⁠there is military materiel on ⁠board," ​Iljin remarked.

The ship is on a US sanctions list, according to a search of the Open Sanctions website.

The Border Guard later said the crew of the Sparta II was evacuating into a life raft and rescue boat.

"The [Ukraine] war is spilling over into our neighbouring areas," wrote Finnish Prime Minister Petteri Orpo on X.

Ukraine has the right to fight against the aggressor," he added.

The Finnish government has put temporary curbs on aviation and maritime traffic in the eastern Gulf of Finland.

The Defense Ministry stated Finland had informed its allies about the incident.

#105237. Astronomers just discovered a rare triple star system 28 light-years away, and they have ‘no clean explanation for how it got here’

📅 23 Nov 2026 • ⏱️ 6m • 📚 Deep Dive (1262 w)

Astronomers just discovered a rare triple star system 28 light-years away, and they have ‘no clean explanation for how it got here’

📅 23 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 6 min read (1262 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Space

⏱️ ~6 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • A triple system containing a dim red dwarf star and not one but two white dwarfs has been fortuitously discovered just 28 light-years away from our solar system.
  • "We were actually looking for planets," Étienne Artigau of the Trottier Institute for Research on Exoplanets at the Université de Montréal, who led the discovery, said in a statement.
  • So surprising that there are no similar systems within at least 100 light-years.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

A triple system containing a dim red dwarf star and not one but two white dwarfs has been fortuitously discovered just 28 light-years away from our solar system.

"We were actually looking for planets," Étienne Artigau of the Trottier Institute for Research on Exoplanets at the Université de Montréal, who led the discovery, said in a statement. "Instead, we found something much more surprising.".

So surprising that there are no similar systems within at least 100 light-years. Furthermore, the configuration of the system seems impossible. "This system should not exist," added Montreal's Patrick Dufour. "We have no clean explanation for how it got here.".

This triple system has been called Welopō'ai, which is a portmanteau of two Hawaiian words that means a 'path of family traits', and to understand the mystery behind it requires astronomers to figure out the history of the three objects.

A white dwarf is what remains when a star of similar mass to our sun reaches the end of its life. As it begins to run low on hydrogen for nuclear fusion reactions in its core, the star's energy generation begins to falter and its interior starts to contract under gravity. This has the effect of raising the temperature throughout the star, causing an outer shell of hydrogen to ignite its own fusion reactions. The star promptly bloats to become a red giant tens or even hundreds of millions of kilometers across.

Recent findings suggest that soon enough the star ceases fusion reactions completely. The star's outer layers are shed and they expand out into space, while its core contracts to become an inert white dwarf with a diameter similar to Earth but with a mass generally between half and two-thirds of a solar mass.

Therefore, the Welopō'ai system was once a triple system with two sun-like stars plus the red dwarf. Now the two sun-like stars have undergone this stage of star death while their companion red dwarf continues to linger, since its low mass bequeaths it a longer life because it does not use up its core hydrogen as promptly.

One of the white dwarfs orbits the red dwarf at a distance of 129.3 astronomical units (19.3 billion kilometers or 12 billion miles) and takes about 1,000 years to complete one orbit. This white dwarf and the red dwarf were previously known, and Artigau's team had been using the SPectropolarimètre InfraROUge (SPIRou) instrument on the Canada–France–Hawaii Telescope atop Mauna Kea to search for planets orbiting the red dwarf when they noticed something highly unusual.

Industry observers note that SPIRou discovers planets by measuring how much their gravity tugs on their host star. Think of a star and planet orbiting a kind of gravitational balancing point between them called a center of mass. This center of mass is usually inside the star, since the star is far more massive than the planet, but crucially not at its very center, so the star appears to wobble to and fro around the combined center of mass.

The spectrometer measures this wobble in the form of a Doppler shift in the star's light that can be translated into the velocity at which the star is moving around this center of mass. Astronomers call this a 'radial velocity'. A large gas giant like Jupiter might incur a radial velocity of hundreds of meters per second, while an Earth-mass planet generates a radial velocity of tens of meters.

Yet the object that SPIRou found orbiting close to the red dwarf was creating a huge radial velocity signals of 10 miles (16 kilometers) per second. Whatever it was, it was not a planet. With the help of the eight-meter Gemini North telescope on Hawaii's Mauna Kea, Artigau's team were able to identify the mystery object as a white dwarf.

"The unusual combination of high mass and very low brightness left only one plausible explanation: it was the remnant of a dead star," noted Charles-Antoine Parent, an undergraduate student at Université Laval and a co-author of the study.

White dwarfs are not exactly rare, and even finding two white dwarfs together is not unheard of: WD 0727+482 is a binary white dwarf system 37 light-years away, for example. To encounter two white dwarfs in a triple system with a regular star though is a precious find.

Industry observers note that the reason being that the masses of white dwarfs are not generally well defined. Yet their masses are not random; they are directly connected to the mass of the star that produced them.

Thanks to the newly discovered white dwarf being separated from the red dwarf by about 4.6 astronomical units (688 million kilometers/428 million miles) – that's closer than Jupiter orbits our sun – Artigau's team were able to measure their masses to within an uncertainty of less than 1%. They found that the red dwarf has a mass 42% that of our sun and the newly discovered white dwarf has a mass 62% that of our sun. When the white dwarf was a regular star it would have had a mass 40% greater than our sun. The second more distant white dwarf orbits the pair of them.

The Welopō'ai system is therefore a good system for testing our models of stellar evolution that dictate how massive a white dwarf should be. If we know the white dwarf's mass with high precision, scientists can also use that as a starting point from which to explore the extreme physics of the white dwarf's condensed matter, which is being held up and prevented from contracting any further by something called electron degeneracy pressure – the unwillingness of negatively charged electrons to crush down any further and merge with positively charged protons to form neutrons. That takes the extra gravity from a more massive star to form a neutron star.

In a recent development, so why should Welopō'ai not exist? The trouble is that when stars turn into red giants they really stir things up. Even if the red giant didn't expand out as far as the red dwarf, the expansion should have destabilized the red dwarf's orbit and potentially even caused it to crash into the red giant. Yet here the red dwarf is in a happily stable orbit like nothing had happened.

According to recent reports, "That is the question driving our next observations," said Dufour. It is hoped that further, more detailed, measurements of the gravitational interactions between the three members of the Welopō'ai system will help the team disentangle the evolutionary history of the trio to better understand their orbits and how the red dwarf survived. And because they are so relatively close to us, we have the advantage of being able to make high-precision measurements.

"Discoveries like this remind us that our own cosmic neighborhood still contains remarkable surprises," remarked Artigau. "Even when we're searching for planets, our universe often has something completely unexpected waiting for us.".

The discovery of the Welopō'ai triple system is described in a paper published on Nov. 19 in Astronomy & Astrophysics.

Sources indicate that keith Cooper is a freelance science journalist and editor in the United Kingdom, and has a degree in physics and astrophysics from the University of Manchester. He's the author of "The Contact Paradox: Challenging Our Assumptions in the Search for Extraterrestrial Intelligence" (Bloomsbury Sigma, 2020) and has written articles on astronomy, space, physics and astrobiology for a multitude of magazines and websites.
